rows.grounds: compound of muni (sage) and indra (lord); nominative plural subject
inclusive particle extending the claim to additional authorities
pronominal adjective indicating additional sages distinct from those previously mentioned
compound of prakṛti (nature), puruṣa (spirit), and sthāna (station/place); object of recognition
adjective qualifying the station as stainless or untainted

items.question: Do other great sages also acknowledge a pure station of prakṛti and puruṣa?
premises: Great sages are recognized authorities in this teaching.
Other sages, in addition to those previously mentioned, hold a related view.
They acknowledge a station associated with prakṛti and puruṣa that is pure.
items.inference: The pure station of prakṛti and puruṣa is affirmed by other great sages as well.
uncertainties: The specific identity of the other sages is not stated in this verse.
The exact doctrinal sense of sthāna (place, state, or level) depends on the broader context.
items.plain_english: Other great sages also recognize the pure station of prakṛti and puruṣa.
